entries.proposition: Direction determines the phenotype. Two substitutions at one residue, A398E and A398V, have opposite effects on channel function and on seizures: the gain-of-function A398E patient developed generalised tonic-clonic seizures controlled on medication, while two unrelated A398V patients (partial loss of function) had developmental delay and microcephaly with no seizures.
entries.snippet: Seizures were also absent in the two unrelated patients with the A398V variant, correlating with the lack of hyperexcitability in the A398V NEURON model.

entries.proposition: The authors' reading of seizure risk from this and the earlier paper: substantial gain of Cav3.3 function leads to seizures, whereas both gain and loss of function can cause neurodevelopmental disease. This is a correlation across few patients; one gain-of-function patient (M1425V) had staring spells and no seizures.
entries.snippet: The hyperexcitability of TRN neurons expressing the gain-of-function variants correlates with the seizure phenotype in the patients with the M1425I and A398E variants.

entries.proposition: Generalisation by the authors: loss-of-function variants in voltage-gated calcium channels are linked to less severe developmental disorders with epilepsy a less frequent comorbidity than for gain-of-function variants. A T-type blocker would therefore be a mechanism-matched intervention for gain-of-function carriers and a mismatched or possibly harmful one for loss-of-function carriers: the genotype decides, and the paper shows no drug data of any kind.
entries.snippet: Generally, loss-of-function variants in voltage-gated calcium channels are linked to less severe cases of ID/DD, and epilepsy is less often a comorbidity compared to gain-of-function variants linked to ID/DD.

entries.proposition: Patient 4 (M1425V) had moderate intellectual disability, attention deficit and later psychosis with life-long staring spells but no seizures, a gain-of-function carrier without epilepsy, with behavioural and sleep abnormalities; the authors note the milder phenotype compared with M1425I correlates with milder gating effects.
entries.snippet: The 25-year-old male patient 4 with the p.(Met1425Val) variant had microcephaly, moderate ID, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, rigidity, and hyperacusis.
entries.anchor: Results, Four unrelated patients with a neurodevelopmental disorder

entries.proposition: Limits stated by the authors: the TRN neuron result is a computer simulation (heterozygous state mimicked as a 1:1 mix of channels) and the patients' mechanism of disease (calcium toxicity versus altered firing) is not resolved; further animal-model research is needed to say which pathways underlie the diverse phenotypes.
entries.snippet: Further research in animal models will have to elucidate which pathways, underlying the diverse neurodevelopmental phenotype, are affected by reduced versus increased CaV3.3 activity.

entries.proposition: A figure legend states that the disease-associated substitutions A398E/V and M1425V/I have distinct effects on calcium channel activation.
entries.snippet: Distinct effects on calcium channel activation of CACNA1I disease-associated amino acid substitutions A398E/V and M1425V/I.

entries.proposition: A figure legend states that all Cav3.3 variants left-shift the voltage dependence of inactivation.
entries.snippet: All CaV3.3 variants left-shift the voltage dependence of inactivation.

entries.proposition: A figure legend states that three variants left-shift the window current while the A398V variant completely abolishes it.
entries.snippet: Three CaV3.3 variants left-shift the window current, while the A398V completely abolishes the window current.

entries.proposition: A figure legend states that the computer modelling predicts increased electrical activity at rest and after hyperpolarising pulses for three variants and quiescence at rest for the A398V variant.
entries.snippet: NEURON computer modelling predicts increased electrical activity at rest and in response to hyperpolarizing pulses for three variants of CaV3.3 and quiescence at rest for the A398V variant.

entries.proposition: Figure 2 read as an image (cells expressing the channel): peak density is smaller for A398V (about minus 18 against minus 50 pA/pF; one star), not different for A398E, M1425V or M1425I; half-activation is more negative for A398E (about minus 49 against minus 38 mV; four stars), M1425V (about minus 50 against minus 38) and M1425I (about minus 49), and less negative for A398V (about minus 34 mV; two stars).
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2G, I, K, M: Ipeak A398V about -18 vs WT about -50 pA/pF (*); V1/2 act A398E about -49, M1425V about -50, M1425I about -49 vs WT about -38 mV (****); A398V about -34 (**).

entries.proposition: Figure 3 read as an image (kinetics): the inactivation time constant is about 190 ms for A398E against about 80 ms for wild type (two stars) and about 25 to 45 ms for A398V (stars), and about 330 to 410 ms for M1425V and about 480 to 730 ms for M1425I against about 120 to 190 ms (stars); the deactivation time constant at minus 60 mV is about 40 ms for A398E, about 42 for M1425V and about 60 for M1425I against about 5 to 7 ms for wild type (three stars), and about 1.5 ms for A398V.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 3B, C, E, F: tau inactivation A398E about 190 vs WT about 80 ms; A398V about 25-45; M1425V about 330-410, M1425I about 480-730 vs WT about 120-190; tau deactivation at -60 mV A398E about 40, M1425V about 42, M1425I about 60 vs WT about 6 ms (***), A398V about 1.5.

entries.proposition: Figure 6 read as an image (simulated reticular-nucleus neuron): the A398E, M1425V and M1425I simulations fire more often at rest than the wild-type simulation and produce longer, denser bursts after the hyperpolarising pulse, while the A398V simulation is silent at rest and fires a single spike after the pulse; the wild-type simulation fires about 14 spikes in the first 3000 ms.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 6A-H: AE, MV, MI fire more at rest and longer bursts after the pulse than WT; AV silent at rest, single spike after the pulse; WT about 14 spikes in 3 s.
